title: Staged concurrent scorer with dynamic token caps and graceful aborts
creator: Mateo Rivera
description:
Problem: The reranking endpoint still shows a long right tail for p95/p99 latency under mixed workloads (short interactive queries + long document scoring). Current monolithic batching and a single token cap cause head-of-line blocking and inefficient KV cache prefetching. This ticket introduces a staged concurrent scorer that separates requests into latency-sensitive and throughput lanes, applies dynamic token caps per-lane, and implements graceful abort/fallback policies when soft timeouts elapse.

Design summary:
- Lane separation: classify incoming rerank requests at ingress into two lanes: 'interactive' (low token budgets, strict latency SLO) and 'bulk' (longer token budgets, throughput-optimized). Classification will use request headers + heuristics (prompt tokens, client tag).
- Dynamic token caps: per-lane token ceilings computed from running capacity signals (GPU utilization, batch queue length) and a configurable per-customer budget. Caps are enforced by the request router and within the serving runtime to bound KV cache memory use.
- Soft timeouts & graceful aborts: implement a soft deadline at the scorer stage. If soft timeout triggers, scorer returns partial scores (best-effort) and the router attempts a fallback to a cheaper / lower-seq-length model variant or returns a best-effort ranked list with confidence flags. Hard timeout still applies to prevent resource starvation.
- Parallelization: within each lane, requests are grouped into microbatches using deadline-aware packing. Microbatches are dispatched to multiple scorer workers in parallel (worker pool sharding) rather than single-thread serial scoring. Implement token-aware worker assignment so long-token requests are distributed to avoid stalling short requests.
- KV-prefetch prioritization: prioritize KV prefetch for interactive lane requests; bulk lane prefetch runs opportunistically. Add bounded prefetch queue to avoid unbounded memory growth.

Trade-offs considered:
- Extra complexity in router and worker assignment vs. measurable latency improvements. We accept added scheduling complexity because it isolates tail latency sources.
- Returning partial/approximate results on soft timeout improves availability but can reduce quality; we will mark these responses with confidence metadata and track rollback if downstream evals degrade.
- Prefetch prioritization may slightly reduce bulk throughput; we'll tune thresholds during canary.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement feature flag + default-off.
2) Unit tests + integration tests in staging.
3) Canary traffic (5% of rerank requests) for a single low-risk customer cohort. Monitor latencies, IRR, and quality regressions on held-out evals.
4) Gradual ramp with fallback thresholds and an automated rollback if quality regressions >1.5% or errors spike >0.5%.

Acceptance criteria and metrics: see acceptance_criteria field.

Notes: This ticket depends on prior KV-prefetch work and microbatch primitives (see dependencies). Full design doc in Confluence (link below).
acceptance_criteria: p95 token-generation latency for interactive lane reduced by at least 20ms in staging compared to baseline
no more than 1% drop in rerank precision@10 on customer evaluation set; automated regression tests pass
system-level resource usage remains within existing quotas (GPU memory increase <8%)
soft-timeout responses annotated with confidence metadata and surfaced in console metrics
feature toggles exist to disable lane separation and graceful aborts independently
steps: Add request classifier in router (header heuristics + token-length threshold)
Implement lane-aware token cap calculation service (stateless, uses metrics API)
Extend microbatch packing to be deadline-aware and token-aware
Add worker pool sharding and token-aware assignment in runtime
Implement soft timeout handling and fallback flow (cheaper model or partial results)
Integrate KV-prefetch prioritization and bounded prefetch queue
End-to-end tests, performance benchmarks, and canary rollout
Dashboarding: add per-lane latency, fallback counts, and quality regression alerts
